title: Polyphasic Sleep
author: InsolentCoolRadio
selftext:
Half awake. I’m setting a timer and sleeping for 20 minutes to get up and see if Space Grok (Grok via Cursor) needs anything as it’s working on my Unity animations. Then I’m going back to sleep. I’ll probably repeat this cycle for a few hours.

To what extent is your sleep schedule dependent on AI rate limits and/or agentic coding sprints?

I read in ‘Hackers: Heroes of the Computer Revolution’ that back in the day (like when they had punch cards)programmers used to “phase shift” their sleep cycles because they were awake for a long time every day, which led to a cultural environment where it was normal for people to have bespoke sleep cycles.

I’m wondering to what extent history is rhyming.

Life is a brutal and cruel roguelike. Pick the least horrible option 🧮🤖🏭🤖🫩🤖🏗️🤖👾

comments.author: glass_wheel
comments.body: Used to phase shift? I love the 28 hour day ^~^ but that's not dependent on any external system, that's just a benefit of flexibility.

replies.author: InsolentCoolRadio
replies.body:
That’s what they called it in the book

They’d prepend an adverb with the time of day like “Morning Phase” or “Lunch Phase”

I listened to it a long time ago, but that part really stuck with me

I attempted the ideas from The 5AM Club, but I might be too feral for that

A rolling 28 sounds awesome 🤘
